title: Andrea da Birago to Francesco Sforza, Pavia, 28 February 1448 (BnF italien 1585 f. 33), with its clear duplicate f. 32

plaintext.source: f. 32, the writer's clear duplicate of the same letter, mounted above it

transcription.notes: 513 signs in 11 lines (first on the salutation line), word gaps marked as the scribe left them; two shapes uncertain (L06, L09). Subagent transcription, checked here on L01-L02 and L07.

system.summary: Simple substitution, one sign per letter, with a sign for et and one code sign for Francesco Piccinino (key DECODE R5316).
system.sibling_key: Birago's own key sheet, ASMi Carteggio Sforzesco cart. 1597 no. 16 (DECODE R5316).

prior_solution.where: f. 32, the clear duplicate of the same letter on the same mount (BnF ital. 1585); key sheet R5316 in Milan, not connected to the letter before

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau asked for lead 1546 to be worked (check f. 32 as a crib, look for a Birago key, attempt it) and supplied the DECODE cookie.

solution.what: Leaf-by-leaf check of the 1447-48 Milan series: ital. 1585 f. 33 the only cipher leaf with no decipherment beside it (lead 1546).
DECODE metadata searched for Birago: only the 16th-c. Lodovico Birago.
Fetched ASMi cart. 1597 nos. 1-40 key records (DECODE R5301-R5340) and read their headings: no. 16 (R5316) is headed 'Andreas Biragus'.
Key applied to the first cipher line: 'sono stati da mi dui famigli de orlando palauiciano et hame dicto per parte sua...', the opening of f. 32: f. 33 is the ciphered duplicate of f. 32.
513 cipher signs transcribed sign by sign as key letters (subagent), decoded with decode.py; 0 signs off the key, 2 uncertain shapes.
Decryption compared with f. 32 word by word: 35 spelling or small-form differences, no content difference; the cipher's 'carigo' settles f. 32's hard word 'incharicho'.

outcome.method_basis: The writer's clear duplicate of the same letter (f. 32) is mounted above the cipher; the cipher was transcribed and decoded with Birago's own key sheet, found on DECODE (R5316, unconnected before), and checked word by word against f. 32.
outcome.fraction_read_source: texts/f33_decryption.txt: 513 of 513 cipher signs on the key and in sense (2 uncertain shapes fixed by sense)

texts.label: Andrea da Birago to Francesco Sforza, Pavia, 28 Feb 1448 (f. 33, with its clear duplicate f. 32)
texts.summary: Orlando Pallavicino, reconciled with Sforza, asks Birago's help to get home; Birago will give it on Sforza's commission, all the more since the Milanese mean to give Francesco Piccinino whatever he asks, Orlando's lands included.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences line by line against the decode and the clear duplicate f. 32; agrees throughout except spelling; two sign shapes uncertain, fixed by sense.

gaps.item: two sign shapes (L06 c/g in darghelo, L09 i in milano)

credits.note: Birago's clear duplicate f. 32 and his key sheet (ASMi cart. 1597 no. 16, DECODE R5316).

outcome.notes: Lead 1546. The key sheet on DECODE had no description; its connection to this letter is new.
